What benefit does a San Francisco HQ offer if you are not a frontier AI lab?
items.summary: I am struggling to see the benefit of basing your startup in SF if you are not a frontier AI lab? It seems to me that the talent quality outside of these frontier labs and associated companies (companies founded by alumni) may fundamentally be no better than anywhere else in the world, but demand twice as much as the "SF premium" only to leave after 6 months for the next big startup. Because of this, I could probably get more bang for my buck starting my company in another tech hub, such as LA, London, Berlin or Tallinn?

items.summary: I was finding that managing multiple agent threads with walls of text was getting tiring and inefficient for me and that I wanted a more visual way to interact with my agents, so I built Lynx. Lynx lets you quickly build fully custom interfaces connected to your data sources (e.g. via MCP or API) and trigger agents running on your machine from them (e.g. with Claude Code or Codex). I built it as an experiment but have found myself doing 80-90% of my work from inside Lynx.
